The two are not symmetric because the operator supplies the receipt by hand: a receipt lacking the ownership key falls through to the unit attribute, and the mutant makes it read owned, which skips the identity verification and prompts a session whose identity was never checked. Narrow, since every receipt the launcher itself writes carries the key.

findings.title: The retry command accepts an empty prompt without refusing
findings.why_it_matters: The retry reuses the shared launch flags, where the prompt defaults to the empty string and its help text describes only what an omitted prompt does to the launch command. A retry exists solely to re-send a task, so an invocation without a prompt types an empty line into a pane the operator just cleared and then reports the prompt as undelivered, consuming the retry route's one safe attempt on a session that is still idle. Every documented example passes a prompt, so the shipped argument contract is looser than the documented one.

findings.title: The retry command's refusal classes share one exit code with different output
findings.why_it_matters: The command exits 1 for a receipt refusal, for a missing-pane refusal, and for a withheld delivery. A receipt refusal happens before the try block, so standard output is empty; a refusal inside the retry dumps the receipt and re-raises; a withheld delivery dumps the receipt and returns 1. A caller redirecting standard output to a receipt file gets a file that is sometimes empty and sometimes a receipt, all at the same exit code, with nothing in the documentation distinguishing the three.

findings.title: The degraded stub roster binds the guard predicate only on total ingest failure, and the below-floor fixture cannot exercise a genuinely old launcher
findings.why_it_matters: The ingest returns success for a below-floor launcher: it records the error and executes the script anyway, so the stub roster that binds the five newer names never runs in that state. The launcher shipped on the default branch defines none of those five names, so a below-floor install leaves them unbound entirely and any reference would raise a bare name error rather than the named update remedy. Today that is latent, since every reference sits inside one of the six gated commands; the fragility is that the guarantee rests on that gate list staying complete, and the test meant to pin it cannot detect a regression because the fixture builds its below-floor state by installing the current source and rewriting only its version string.

fix_requests.summary: The cross-plugin predicate's contract exists only in changelogs
The write-flag precondition is still hand-threaded per call site
The ingested launcher predicate has no upper bound or capability check

An owned OpenCode launch makes three pane writes with no inspection: the picker never sets the write flag; Parser byte cap can turn a staged draft into a fail-open read; Owned OpenCode launch makes three uninspected pane writes; The retry's liveness gate refuses statuses the module elsewhere classifies as never started; The pane-typing write's timeout is a generic stop that never says the line may have reached the session, unlike the other door; The retry command's refusal classes share one exit code with different output
land exits 0 when a review resubmission is withheld on staged input, while every other resubmission failure exits 4; The new permission field defaults true for legacy run files
The launcher changelog repeats the same overclaim in its own words
The skill claims only one pane write ever skips inspection, but an owned OpenCode launch leaves three writes uninspected

The OpenCode picker guard is the one write site whose write-flag half no test observes; One composer inspection authorises every write send() makes, so a unit's setup slash commands push the task write up to a minute past its guard; The retry refuses any session status but the literal idle, permanently closing the retry route for sessions the launcher's own predicate calls not-started; The one-owner structural guard reads only the launcher tree, so Orchestrate can re-derive the predicate inline undetected; The adopted receipt's ownership read is observed in one direction only

No test drives Orchestrate's repaired sender with a paneless unit, so its pane clause is unobserved; The staged-retry predicate's pane clause survives deletion, repeating the cycle-1 counter-case shape; The degraded stub roster binds the guard predicate only on total ingest failure, and the below-floor fixture cannot exercise a genuinely old launcher
The run-file contract observing test compares two literals rather than exercising the gate its name describes

The launcher suite still pins the companion floor in lockstep; The receipt shape derives ownership from the receipt it is replacing, not from the ownership just computed; One local name is reused for two unrelated types in one function, and the gate cannot see it; The launch receipt key set is undocumented and accepts a dead alias; The retry command accepts an empty prompt without refusing
The Orchestrate skill overstates the downgrade refusal to all older versions
The unit reader promises forward tolerance the run loader prevents
